title: ssh: Simplify sequence number tracking during first KEX
description:
Use the standard ssh_message_info_t struct as used for encrypted
packets to store the sequence number, and increment it in the main
ssh_dissect_key_exchange function. This avoids doing extra bookkeeping
inside the key exchange functions, and greatly simplifies the peer_data
struct.

This also means that (non-strict KEX extension) handshakes that
have SSG_MSG_IGNORE or SSH_MSG_DEBUG messages before the first
KEX completes will correctly increment the sequence number. Thus
matching the behavior of actual SSH implementations with regards to
the Terrapin attack.
